terms.meaning: The language that tells the browser how a page should look.
A styling tool that provides small named style classes.
A set of steps that describe how an animation changes over time.
The highlight shown around the element a keyboard user is on.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Base setup and page colors
sections.what: Sets up the style system, a set of named colors, the default page background and text color, and a slim scrollbar.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives every page one starting look before individual screens add their own styles.
sections.watch_out: Two color sets exist, one here and one in the Tailwind configuration, so a change in one may not show up where the other is used.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Shared button, input, card, and status styles
sections.what: Defines the shared look for primary and secondary buttons, input boxes, cards, and text colors for valid, warning, and error states.
sections.why: Likely reason: reusable named styles keep screens consistent and short.
sections.watch_out: The input style removes the default focus outline and replaces it with a red ring, so keyboard users depend on that ring being visible.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Slide-up and glow keyframes
sections.what: Defines two motion steps: a slide-up that fades in while moving up, and a pulsing green glow.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the motion effects used by the animation classes below.
sections.watch_out: The glow repeats forever, so using it on many items at once can be distracting.

sections.name: .animate-fade-in
sections.title: Fade-in animation class
sections.what: Makes any element that uses this class fade in over about a third of a second.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is a common, gentle entrance effect.

sections.name: .animate-slide-up
sections.title: Slide-up animation class
sections.what: Makes an element slide up a short distance while fading in over about four-tenths of a second.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is a common entrance effect.

sections.name: .animate-glow
sections.title: Pulsing glow animation class
sections.what: Makes an element pulse with a green glow, repeating without end.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It likely draws attention to something active.
sections.watch_out: It repeats without end, so use it sparingly.

sections.name: .tabular-nums
sections.title: Aligned number columns class
sections.what: Makes digits take equal width so numbers in a column line up when scanned.
sections.why: Likely reason: so columns of costs are easy to compare.

summary: The main stylesheet that sets the app's base colors and defines the shared button, input, card, status, and animation styles.
purpose: Gives the whole app a consistent look beyond the individual class names used in components.
why: Likely reason: reusable named styles avoid repeating long lists of classes on every screen. The top comment says the look is inspired by the Nothing and Teenage Engineering style, but the body rule uses the Bain palette. The reason for mixing them is not stated in the code.
how: First it loads the Tailwind style system. Then it sets named colors, the default page background and text color, and a slim scrollbar. Next it defines shared styles for buttons, inputs, cards, and status text. Last it defines a few animations: fade-in, slide-up, and a pulsing glow.
inputs: The Tailwind style system and the color names from the Tailwind configuration.
outputs: Global styles that apply to every page, plus named classes that components can use.
risks: Two color sets exist, one here and one in the Tailwind configuration, so a change in one may not appear where the other is used. The input style removes the default focus outline, so keyboard users rely on the red ring being visible.
debug: If a style does not appear, check that the class is defined here and that the color name exists in the Tailwind configuration. If page colors look wrong, check the body rule here and the body classes in index.html.
